note: Method lives in .claude/skills/consensus-guide/SKILL.md. theViabilityVerdict:
ASKED AND ANSWERED 2026-09-07: NO. THIS TOPIC IS NOT VIABLE AS A CONSENSUS GUIDE, AND IT SHOULD NOT BE COLLECTED AS ONE. It is viable as a REGISTER-LED guide, which is a different and better page. A config saying so is the correct outcome here.

THE METHOD COUNTS HOW MANY INDEPENDENT SOURCES NAME A VENUE. That measurement only means something when the population of venues is large enough that sources have to CHOOSE between them. Here it is not. Four kashrut authorities between them license roughly thirty-five to forty-five sit-down kosher restaurants in the whole of London, and the certifier publishes the complete list for free. A consensus ranking over that population would be measuring which ten of about forty restaurants four listicles happened to mention - and those four listicles largely name the same ten, because they are the ten with a website and a PR.

THE REGISTER IS THE LIST. That is the sentence this whole config exists to deliver. KLBD's own restaurant register carries 39 entries with an address, a phone number and a meat/dairy/parve label on every one. Nothing this project could build by counting listicles improves on it, and a guide that ranked venues by citation count would be quietly telling readers that the un-cited two thirds of the register do not exist.

WHAT THE PASS ACTUALLY FOUND - 6 countable editorial domains, and the two biggest names on this site are not among them:
  TIER A  0  No judged restaurant award. The British Kebab Awards' kosher category is part public vote and judges ONE DISH - see awardBodiesChecked.
  TIER B  3  The Jewish Chronicle, Jewish News, DesignMyNight. The first two are community mastheads and NEITHER publishes a ranked best-of.
  TIER C  3  London x London, Walk Eat London, UK Jewish Life. All three are thin, stale or borderline - see editorialLists.
  TIER D  COLLECTABLE at no cost, but thin and much of it is not restaurant criticism - see theVideoFinding.
  TIER E  blocked. Reddit refuses curl and the browser alike.

TIME OUT AND THE INFATUATION DO NOT COVER THIS TOPIC AT ALL. Verified 2026-09-07 by direct search: neither publishes a London kosher guide. Time Out carries 46 source records across this site, more than any other domain, and zero here. That absence is the sourcing problem stated in one line, and it is the reason the SERP fills up with directories instead.

THE SERP IS DIRECTORIES, NOT EDITORIAL. The first page of both restaurant queries is thekosheratlas.com, totallyjewishtravel.com, kosherinlondon.co.uk, gokosher.com, eatkosher.co.uk, Tripadvisor and TheFork. A filterable database is not an opinion and must not be counted as one - the same call made on dinehalal.uk in halal.json and blackeatsldn.com in caribbean.json. Two of the remaining slots are domains this project has ALREADY excluded on other topics.

RECOMMENDATION: do not run the consensus pipeline on this topic. Build the page from the certifier registers, with the four axes in theDistinctions carried per venue, and use the handful of editorial voices for PROSE and for what is worth eating - not for ranking. If Rob wants a ranked guide anyway, that is his call to make with this verdict in front of him; per ask-dont-publish-gaps the question goes to him rather than onto the page.
theAccuracyProblem:
GETTING KOSHER STATUS WRONG IS NOT A RANKING ERROR, IT IS A HARM. A reader who eats somewhere on the strength of this guide is relying on it for a religious dietary requirement, and for an observant reader a wrong call is not a disappointing meal - it is a transgression they cannot undo. Every other topic on this site fails softly. This one does not. Same rule as halal.json, different specifics.

THE STATUSES THAT SOURCES ROUTINELY CONFLATE:
  1. CERTIFIED UNDER SUPERVISION - a named kashrut authority (KLBD, KF Kosher, Kedassia, SKA) licenses the establishment and its hechsher can be checked against that authority's own register. Verifiable, and the ONLY status this guide may call kosher.
  2. 'KOSHER-STYLE' - salt beef, bagels, chopped liver, latkes, a Jewish menu and no supervision at all. IT IS NOT KOSHER. This is the single most dangerous category on the topic because it looks like the thing it is not, and because the food is often excellent, which is exactly why writers include it.
  3. 'KOSHER OPTIONS' / 'KOSHER-FRIENDLY' - a mainstream kitchen with some dishes an observant diner might eat. Not kosher, and not even kosher-style.

A GUIDE THAT PRINTS ALL THREE AS 'KOSHER' IS WRONG IN A WAY THAT MATTERS. CARRY THE STATUS PER VENUE, SOURCED TO THE AUTHORITY THAT SAYS IT, AND NEVER UPGRADE A VENUE'S OWN CLAIM INTO A CERTIFICATION. A listicle saying 'kosher' is not evidence. A certifier's register is.

AND UNLIKE HALAL, THE PRIMARY EVIDENCE IS EXCELLENT. This is the one piece of good news in the topic. Every certifier publishes a register, they are free, current and specific, and they carry the meat/dairy label as their own field. The halal guide had to build its status axis venue by venue against a scatter of venue websites; here it can be lifted from four register pages. USE THEM. Do not build this axis from any listicle, including the good ones.

A LICENCE IS ALSO PERISHABLE. Establishments gain and lose supervision, and the authorities publish that: the SKA's own feed carries 'The following establishment is no longer under the supervision of the Sephardi Kashrut Authority', and KLBD publishes dated monthly update PDFs listing newly licensed restaurants. RE-CHECK THE REGISTER AT PUBLICATION, not at collection, and give the page a visible checked-on date. A certification claim that was true in March is not evidence in November.

RECORD, DO NOT RULE ON, WHAT THE COMMUNITY IS DIVIDED OVER. Which hechsherim a given reader accepts is a matter of communal practice and rabbinic authority, and it is not this site's place to arbitrate it. Name the supervising authority per venue and let the reader apply their own standard. NEVER write that one authority is stricter, better or more reliable than another, and never imply a venue is 'more kosher' than another. Say who certifies it, and stop.
theAccuracyProblemConfirmed:
THE 2026-09-07 SOURCE PASS PROVED THIS SECTION RIGHT, IN THE FIRST PAGE OF RESULTS, ON A DOMAIN THIS PROJECT ALREADY TRUSTS.

walkeatlondon.com - registered TIER C in data/sources.json, and named in data/serp/README.md as the example of a business blog that belongs IN - publishes 'Top 10 Jewish and Kosher Restaurants in Central London'. Its ten include Bubala, Monty's Deli and Tabun Kitchen. Its own text says of them 'While not strictly kosher', 'not fully kosher' and 'not strictly kosher'. So the page is honest INSIDE the entries and wrong in the HEADLINE, which is precisely how a reader gets misled: the list is titled kosher, the caveat is three paragraphs down, and the venue is in the list either way. It also has no byline and no date, and it places Sami's on 'Edgware Road' when the KLBD register puts Sami's in Edgware, HA8 - two different places about eight miles apart.

SO: THE STATUS AXIS CANNOT BE LIFTED FROM ANY LISTICLE IN THIS CORPUS, INCLUDING THE ONES THE README HOLDS UP AS GOOD. It comes from the registers. This is the same finding halal.json recorded about havehalalwilltravel.com and the same one fried-chicken.json recorded about Hungry Soles printing a flat 'Halal' against Morley's. Three topics, three trusted sources, the same error. It is the normal failure mode of this subject rather than an unlucky page.

THE OPPOSITE ERROR IS ALSO PRESENT. London x London (Feb 2023) names Delicatessen, Zest and Met Su Yan; UK Jewish Life names Deli 98, Tony Page @ Island Grill and One Ashbourne. NONE of those six is on the KLBD restaurant register read on 2026-09-07. That does not make them uncertified - they may be under KF Kosher, Kedassia or SKA, or they may have closed or lost supervision since. IT MEANS THE LISTICLE AND THE REGISTER DISAGREE, and the register wins. Every venue that reaches print has to be found on a named authority's list or marked unconfirmed.
theDistinctions:
VERIFIED 2026-09-07 AGAINST PRIMARY SOURCES, NOT ASSUMED. The brief named three axes; the pass confirms all three and adds a fourth that turns out to matter more than one of them. These are the fields the guide must carry per venue and must never conflate.

1. CERTIFIED vs 'KOSHER-STYLE'. CONFIRMED REAL AND CONFIRMED CONFLATED - see theAccuracyProblemConfirmed. This is the load-bearing one.

2. MEAT (FLEISHIG) vs DAIRY (MILCHIG) vs PARVE. CONFIRMED, AND IT IS THE REGISTER'S OWN FIELD RATHER THAN ONE THIS PROJECT INVENTED. KLBD labels every single entry: 'Bagels Bar (Dairy)', 'Bagels Bar Grill House (Meat)', 'SurFin Poke (Meat/Parev)', 'Sushi Hinoki (Meat/Parev)'. Of the 39 entries read, roughly 21 are Meat, 14 Dairy and 4 Meat/Parev.

   WHY IT IS A HARD PLANNING FACT AND NOT A TECHNICALITY: a kosher kitchen is one or the other, so a dairy restaurant serves NO meat at all and a meat restaurant serves NO milk - no butter, no cheese, no milk in the coffee, no dessert containing cream. A reader who wants a steak and a reader who wants a pizza cannot eat in the same room, and a group containing both has to split up. Nothing on a restaurant's frontage tells them which it is.

   THE SHARPEST EXAMPLES ARE PAIRS OF THE SAME BRAND, DOORS APART, AND THIS IS THE DETAIL THE GUIDE SHOULD LEAD THE SECTION WITH: Bagels Bar (Dairy) at 84 Brent Street and Bagels Bar Grill House (Meat) at 86 Brent Street, Hendon - next door to each other. Novellino (Dairy) at 103 Golders Green Road and Novellino Bistro (Meat) at 111a-113 Golders Green Road - the same side of the same street. Getting these two the wrong way round is the most likely single error in the whole guide and it is also the most useful thing the guide can tell a reader.

   CHALAV YISRAEL AND GLATT ARE NOT DIFFERENTIATORS WITHIN THE KLBD SET. The register's own header states: 'All milk products used by KLBD dairy restaurants are Chalav Yisrael. All meaty restaurants are Glatt.' So do not print these per venue as though some KLBD venues have them and others do not. They MAY differ between authorities - check before writing a word about them.

3. SHOMER SHABBAT / CLOSED FRIDAY NIGHT AND SATURDAY. CONFIRMED FROM PRIMARY SOURCES AND IT IS THE BIGGEST PRACTICAL FACT ON THE PAGE. Novellino's own site: 'Apart from the Jewish Sabbath and festivals, Novellino is open everyday for breakfast, lunch and dinner'. KLBD's register entry for White Fish: 'Eat in and take away Sun-Thurs 12-10pm. Fri take away only.'

   WHY IT OUTRANKS EVERYTHING ELSE FOR A NON-JEWISH READER, WHO IS MOST OF THIS PAGE'S AUDIENCE: Friday night and Saturday lunch are the two busiest restaurant sessions of the week in London, and a supervised kosher restaurant is shut for both. Saturday night opening moves with sunset, so it is late in summer and early in winter. A reader planning a Saturday dinner in Golders Green needs this before they need to know what is good, and no mainstream London guide prints it.

   FESTIVALS CLOSE THEM TOO, and the Jewish calendar is lunar so the dates move every year - Rosh Hashanah, Yom Kippur, Sukkot, Pesach. Passover additionally changes MENUS across the whole scene for eight days. NEVER PRINT A SPECIFIC OPENING TIME OR A FESTIVAL DATE WITHOUT CHECKING IT FOR THE YEAR OF PUBLICATION. Where it cannot be confirmed, print that the venue closes for Shabbat WITHOUT a time rather than guessing - a reader standing outside a shut restaurant is the same class of error as a dead booking link.

4. WHICH AUTHORITY CERTIFIES IT - THE AXIS THE BRIEF DID NOT NAME, AND IT BELONGS BESIDE THE OTHER THREE. There is not one kosher standard in London, there are at least four bodies (see theCertifiers), and observant readers differ over which hechsherim they accept. The directories already treat this as a primary filter - kosherinlondon.co.uk browses 'by location, kashrut authority, and cuisine', totallyjewishtravel.com filters by 'kashrut supervision', thekosheratlas.com prints 'the hechsher' per venue - and UK Jewish Life is the only editorial source found that notes it per venue.

   CARRY IT, AND DO NOT RANK IT. Name the authority, link its register, and let the reader apply their own standard. See the last paragraph of theAccuracyProblem: this is the thing to RECORD, not to rule on. A guide that implied one hechsher was better than another would be taking a side in a communal argument it has no standing in, and would be wrong to.
theCertifiers:
ESTABLISHED 2026-09-07 BY READING THE BODIES' OWN SITES. THE BRIEF NAMED TWO AND CONFLATED THEM. THERE ARE FOUR, AND THE BRIEF'S PAIRING IS WRONG - correcting it here so the error is not inherited.

THE CORRECTION: the brief describes 'the Federation of Synagogues Kashrus Board (Kedassia)'. THOSE ARE TWO DIFFERENT ORGANISATIONS AND NEITHER IS THE OTHER'S TRADING NAME. The Federation of Synagogues' kashrus division is KF KOSHER. Kedassia is the kashrus authority of the UNION OF ORTHODOX HEBREW CONGREGATIONS, a separate body. Writing them as one would put the wrong hechsher against real restaurants, which is exactly the class of error theAccuracyProblem is about.

1. KLBD - KASHRUT DIVISION OF THE LONDON BETH DIN (United Synagogue). THE BIGGEST, AND THE ONE WITH THE BEST REGISTER.
   RESTAURANT REGISTER: https://www.kosher.org.uk/kosher-places/restaurants/ - CONFIRMED LIVE, 39 restaurant and takeaway entries, each with address, phone, website and a Meat/Dairy/Parev label. THIS IS THE SINGLE MOST VALUABLE URL IN THE TOPIC.
   Sibling registers on the same site, all worth reading: /kosher-places/bakeries/, /kosher-places/delis-shops-pop-ups/, /kosher-places/caterers-party-food/, /kosher-places/fishmongers/.
   IT ALSO PUBLISHES DATED MONTHLY UPDATE PDFs listing newly licensed restaurants, e.g. /assets/uploads/2025/11/2025-November-Update.pdf. That is how to catch new openings, and it is dated evidence.
   WATCH THE TWO DOMAINS - THIS IS A TRAP 6 SHAPE. klbdkosher.org is the TRADE site and certifies FOOD MANUFACTURERS AND PRODUCTS, not restaurants; its only search is a product search. Reading it alone would produce a config saying KLBD does not license restaurants, which is false. The consumer site kosher.org.uk is where the restaurants are. A third domain, kosher.london, also resolves to the same division. NOTE ALSO the register answers to BOTH /kosher-places/restaurants/ and /places/restaurants/ - compare name arrays before recording, or it is trap 16.
   SCALE, IN THE BETH DIN'S OWN WORDS (bethdin.org.uk/kashrut): 'The KLBD licenses over 100 caterers, bakeries, restaurants, food manufacturers, bonbonnieres, delis and shops'. Restaurants are a MINORITY of that hundred - do not print 100 as a restaurant count.

2. KF KOSHER - FEDERATION OF SYNAGOGUES BETH DIN (Kehillas Federation). THE SECOND REGISTER, AND IT IS REAL.
   REGISTER: https://kfkosher.org/establishments-catering/ - CONFIRMED LIVE. Roughly 25 establishments named, including Aviv, Mazal, One Ashbourne, Pita, Pizaza, Reubens, Soyo, The Kanteen, Slice, Bracha, Ranch, Mesiba, Logan's, Headroom Cafe, Meats & Treats, The Biltong Factory and The Pillar Hotel (breakfast only). Areas named: Hendon, Golders Green, Edgware, Camden, Central London and Manchester.
   TRAP 12 APPLIES - the list is not London-only. Scope it before counting.
   federation.org.uk/restaurants-establishments/ just redirects the reader to kfkosher.org. Do not record it as a second source.
   NOTE THE OVERLAP WITH KLBD IS SMALL, which is the point: Reubens, Mazal, Soyo, Pita, One Ashbourne and The Kanteen are on the KF list and NOT on the KLBD restaurant register. Neither register alone is the London kosher scene. THE GUIDE NEEDS BOTH, AND THAT IS WHY A LISTICLE THAT NAMES ONLY KLBD VENUES LOOKS WRONG AND A LISTICLE THAT NAMES ONLY KF VENUES ALSO LOOKS WRONG.

3. KEDASSIA - THE JOINT KASHRUS COMMITTEE OF ENGLAND, the kashrus authority of the UNION OF ORTHODOX HEBREW CONGREGATIONS (UOHC). Strictly Orthodox / Charedi, and the authority most associated with Stamford Hill.
   NO PUBLIC WEB REGISTER FOUND, AND THIS IS THE REAL GAP IN THE TOPIC. kedassia.org.uk DOES NOT RESOLVE (DNS failure, 2026-09-07). Its licensees surface only through third parties - jewisheurope.org prints 'Certification: Kedassia' against The Parkside (N15), kosherinlondon.co.uk offers a ?authority=kedassia filter, and UK Jewish Life notes Kedassia per venue. cRc lists it as 'Recommended' with a contact for Rabbi Moshe Chaim E. Padwa.
   SO THE STAMFORD HILL END OF THE SCENE IS THE LEAST DOCUMENTED PART OF THE TOPIC, and it is the part a Charedi-facing guide would be built on. SOMEBODY HAS TO ASK, or find the register by phone. Do NOT infer a Kedassia certification from a directory - a third party repeating a hechsher is not the authority granting it, and this is the one authority where the primary source could not be reached.

4. SKA - SEPHARDI KASHRUT AUTHORITY (Sephardi community; Rosh Va'ad Hakashrut Dayan Yossi David, Director Rabbi David Neifeld).
   REGISTER: https://www.ska.org.uk/licensees - CONFIRMED LIVE. A static list rather than a searchable one. Mostly delis, cafés, caterers, schools and care homes rather than restaurants - the restaurant-shaped entries are few: JW3 Cafe (Finchley Road), Hendon Park Cafe, Bricky's and Kosher Deli (Borehamwood), Menachems and Sam Stoller & Son (Golders Green), Charlotte's Sourdough, Yalla Kitchen, The Churros Factory.
   ITS FEED ALSO PUBLISHES WITHDRAWALS - 'The following establishment is no longer under the supervision of the Sephardi Kashrut Authority'. That is the clearest available evidence that a licence is perishable. Read it before publishing.

AND ONE UNIDENTIFIED AUTHORITY - RESOLVE BEFORE PRINTING IT. Kaifeng's own site says it is 'under both KLBD and MKL supervision'. MKL was NOT identified in this pass and is not one of the four above. Find out what MKL is before any venue is described as being under it, and do not guess at the expansion of the initials.
theCountingProblem:
HOW MANY CERTIFIED KOSHER RESTAURANTS ARE THERE ACTUALLY IN LONDON? ROUGHLY THIRTY-FIVE TO FORTY-FIVE SIT-DOWN RESTAURANTS, AND UNDER SEVENTY EATING PLACES OF ALL KINDS. It is a small, concentrated scene and the guide must say so plainly rather than implying a city-wide field.

THE ARITHMETIC, FROM THE REGISTERS RATHER THAN FROM LISTICLES:
  KLBD restaurant register           39 entries read 2026-09-07
  LESS venues outside Greater London  -3   Balagan (Borehamwood WD6), Pumpernick's (Borehamwood WD6), Yofi (HOVE BN3 - Sussex, sixty miles away)
  LESS second branches of one brand   -6   Bagels Bar, Eli's Pizza, Hummus Bar, Novellino, Sami's and Sushi Haven each appear twice
  = roughly 30 distinct KLBD-licensed London businesses
  PLUS KF Kosher's establishments that are NOT on the KLBD list - Reubens, Mazal, Soyo, Pita, One Ashbourne, The Kanteen, Bracha, Ranch, Mesiba and others, maybe 15 once Manchester and the caterers are scoped out
  PLUS a handful from SKA, and an unknown number from Kedassia whose register could not be reached
  = ROUGHLY 50-70 CERTIFIED KOSHER EATING PLACES IN LONDON, of which perhaps 35-45 are restaurants a reader would sit down in. The rest are bakeries, delis, takeaway counters and caterers.

DO NOT REPEAT THE DIRECTORIES' NUMBERS. thekosheratlas.com claims '112 certified kosher restaurants in London' and totallyjewishtravel.com claims '132 Kosher Supervised Eateries'. Both are far above what the four authorities' own registers support, and both are counting bakeries, shops, hotels, caterers and probably branches. An unverified aggregate is not evidence. If a number goes on the page it must be derived from the registers and dated.

WHAT THAT NUMBER MEANS FOR THE PAGE - THIS IS THE STRUCTURAL DECISION. At about forty restaurants, a 'best of' ranking covers a QUARTER of the field and silently implies the rest are not worth eating at. A near-complete guide is both more useful and more honest, and it is achievable here in a way it is not on pizza or Indian. Recommend: cover the field, order by the reader's real question (meat or dairy, which area, open when), and use the editorial voices to say what is good WITHIN that structure rather than to select what appears at all.

THE GEOGRAPHY IS AS CONCENTRATED AS THE COUNT. On the KLBD register alone: Golders Green, Hendon, Temple Fortune, Edgware and Hampstead Garden Suburb account for the large majority, all in Barnet, and all on essentially two roads - Golders Green Road and Brent Street. Outside that: Tony Page in Marylebone, Tish in Belsize Park, Moss & Maple in West Hampstead, Tasti Pizza in Stamford Hill (N16), Mazal in Camden and Reubens in Baker Street. A reader in south or east London has effectively nothing, and the guide should say that rather than let them discover it. Stamford Hill is under-represented on the registers this pass could read precisely because it is Kedassia territory - see theCertifiers.

BRANCHES: six brands on the KLBD register have two London sites each, and the meat/dairy split sometimes runs BETWEEN the branches rather than across brands (Bagels Bar, Novellino). Chain handling per chains.json, but do NOT collapse a meat branch and a dairy branch into one row - that would destroy the single most useful fact about them.
theOverlapFinding:
TRAP 13 CHECKED 2026-09-07 across all 53 files in data/consensus/. THE WORD 'KOSHER' APPEARS NOWHERE IN THE ENTIRE CORPUS - not once, in any file. This topic is genuinely new ground for the site, which is itself a finding.

URL COLLISION: NONE. None of the seed URLs in data/serp/kosher.txt appears in any consensus file.

EXACTLY ONE REAL VENUE COLLISION, AND IT IS A TRAP 7 CASE:
  HUMMUS BAR is already recorded in data/consensus/middle-eastern.json, named by TWO sources - Secret LDN's falafel guide (secretldn.com/falafel-in-london/) and Mob's best-falafel guide (mob.co.uk/life/the-best-falafel-in-london). It is a KLBD-licensed MEAT restaurant with branches at 82 Golders Green Road and 105 Brent Street, Hendon.
  IT MAY LEGITIMATELY SIT IN BOTH CORPORA - kosher is a certification cutting across cuisines, exactly as halal.json records for Tayyabs. WHAT MUST NOT HAPPEN is printing its middle-eastern citation count on the kosher page. evidence.json records `topics`; check topics.includes('kosher') before printing any number.
  NOTE ALSO that neither falafel source mentions kosher at all. Two sources named this venue for its food and neither knew or said it was certified - which is a small illustration of why this topic needs the registers rather than the listicles.

FALSE POSITIVES IN THE GREP - DO NOT PULL THESE IN:
  'Tish' matches the substring inside BRITISH and TURKISH across seventeen files. The kosher restaurant Tish (Belsize Park, Meat) is NOT in any corpus.
  'Slice' matches pizza-by-the-slice prose in six files. The kosher restaurant Slice (Golders Green, Dairy) is NOT recorded anywhere.
  'Zest' matches 'a zesty salad' in turkish.json. The kosher restaurant Zest at JW3 is not in any corpus.
  'Eat Tokyo Golders Green' (japanese.json) and 'Eat Tokyo G2 Shabu-Shabu' (hot-pot.json, from The Infatuation) are branches of a MAINSTREAM Japanese chain that happen to be in Golders Green. THEY ARE NOT KOSHER. An extractor matching on the area name will pull them in; do not let it.
  'King Neptune Fish & Chip Shop Edgware' (british.json, fish-and-chips.json) matched on the area. Not kosher.
awardBodiesChecked: NO JUDGED KOSHER RESTAURANT AWARD EXISTS FOR LONDON. TIER A IS EMPTY AND CANNOT BE FILLED. That sets the source-mix floor at THREE independent social voices rather than two - see theSourceMixVerdict.

BRITISH KEBAB AWARDS, KOSHER CATEGORY - THE CLOSEST THING, AND IT IS NOT TIER A. Assessed 2026-09-07 and the answer is no, for three separate reasons, any one of which would be enough.

WHAT IT IS, and it is real: an annual awards ceremony founded 2013 by entrepreneur Ibrahim Dogus, 14th edition held 24 February 2026 at Park Plaza Westminster. A KOSHER category was introduced in 2022 BY JEWISH NEWS in collaboration with Dogus. Known winners: REUBENS (Baker Street) took the inaugural 2022 award; MAZAL (Camden) won in 2025 and again in 2026. The 2026 finalists were Balady (Holborn), Bricky's (Borehamwood), Celia's Kitchen (Manchester), Grill on the Hill (Stamford Hill), La Fiesta (Golders Green), Pita (Golders Green), Reubens (Baker Street), Sababa (Borehamwood) and Yakov's Kitchen (Edgware).

WHY IT IS NOT TIER A:
  1. IT IS PART PUBLIC VOTE. The awards' own site says 'Winners are chosen by public vote'; Jewish News says 'through public votes and a panel of judges'. A crowd vote is aggregator-shaped and is the same thing the Tripadvisor rule exists to keep out. This project already made this call on UK Jerk Fest (caribbean.json) and on Wing Fest's People's Choice (fried-chicken.json).
  2. IT JUDGES ONE DISH, NOT A RESTAURANT. The category is 'best kosher shawarma' / kebab. It says nothing about a dairy café, a sushi counter, a pizzeria or a fine-dining room, which is most of the topic. Same limitation Wing Fest has, recorded the same way.
  3. IT IS UK-WIDE (trap 12). Manchester and Borehamwood entries sit in the same shortlist as London ones.

HOW TO USE IT ANYWAY: the FINALIST LIST is a genuinely useful lead, because it surfaces venues no editorial source in this pass names at all - Grill on the Hill (Stamford Hill), Yakov's Kitchen (Edgware), La Fiesta (Golders Green), Balady (Holborn). Chase those and find them on a register. Record the award as a dated fact in a venue's prose ('won the kosher category at the British Kebab Awards in 2025 and 2026') - which is true and interesting - and do NOT record it as a tier-A citation.

TRAP 2 - SYNDICATION. The result reached this pass through Jewish News, The Jewish Chronicle, Time Out, MyLondon and The Star. If it is ever counted, the AWARD is the source. Note that Jewish News CO-CREATED the category, so its award coverage is not an independent opinion about those restaurants and must not be counted as one.

DOMAIN NOTE: britishkebabawards.co.uk does not resolve without the www; use https://www.britishkebabawards.co.uk/. Past winners are published on a sibling domain, brittradeawards.org (e.g. /2024-winners).

A HECHSHER IS NOT AN AWARD. KLBD, KF Kosher, Kedassia and SKA license establishments against a religious standard; they do not rank them and they express no view on whether the food is good. DO NOT RECORD ANY CERTIFIER AS AN AWARD BODY, and do not let a register become a tier-A citation - it would hand every certified venue in London an identical 'award' and destroy the signal entirely.

Michelin - guide.michelin.com is on the permanent403 list in data/sources.json. No London kosher restaurant is expected to hold a star or Bib Gourmand; check the Wikipedia substitute rather than assuming either way.

editorialLists.name: The Jewish Chronicle
editorialLists.verified: 2026-09-07 - LIVE. A standing 'Kosher London' tag page with continuous coverage and a dedicated food writer, VICTORIA PREVER, whose byline appears on ten of the thirteen articles listed. Other bylines: Siam Goorwich, Imogen Garfinkel, Jane Prinsley. NOT REGISTERED in data/sources.json - register it as tier B.
editorialLists.note:
THE COMMUNITY MASTHEAD THIS TOPIC IS BUILT AROUND, AND IT DOES NOT PUBLISH THE SHAPE THIS METHOD COUNTS. Both halves matter.

WHAT IT DOES PUBLISH: single-venue reviews and first looks ('Review: Tavlin's kosher club pops up in Golders Green', 'London dining: Reuben's and Erev reviewed', 'First look: Tony Page Marylebone'), news, chef profiles, and seasonal or annual round-ups ('This year was a great one for kosher food', 'Spring food round up: shishi schnitzel, Josh Katz news and a new NW6 kosher deli', '2026 summer eating guide').

WHAT IT DOES NOT PUBLISH: a ranked or even unranked 'best kosher restaurants in London' list. THIS IS THE EXACT PATTERN caribbean.json recorded for The Voice - the community press covers this food constantly and does not rank it, while the mastheads that do rank things do not cover it at all. Here it is worse than on caribbean, because on caribbean Time Out and The Infatuation both published guides.

SO IT IS A SOURCE FOR PROSE AND FOR FACTS, NOT FOR CITATIONS. Its reviews are the best writing about these restaurants that exists in English and they carry the detail SKILL.md's entry floor asks for. A single-venue review IS a legitimate opinion about that venue and may be recorded as such - what it is not is a list, and it must not be recorded as one. If the year-in-review round-up names a set of venues, THAT is countable.

CHECK FOR A PAYWALL before planning to lean on it, and check whether the round-ups are London-scoped (trap 12) - the JC is a national paper.

editorialLists.name: Jewish News

NOT REGISTERED in data/sources.json - register it as tier B.
editorialLists.note:
THE BEST COUNTABLE EDITORIAL VOICE IN THE TOPIC, with three handling problems, all of them named in its own headlines.

1. TRAP 12 IS IN THE TITLE. 'and they are not all in London'. Scope every round-up before counting a single citation. The page states which are not London, so this is readable rather than guessable.
2. IT IS A SEASONAL 'WHERE TO EAT NOW', NOT A 'BEST OF'. Autumn, winter, summer. These are new-and-notable round-ups, so they skew hard to recent openings and they will NOT name the long-established places a best-of would. Counting several seasons as several sources would also be wrong - one masthead, one opinion, however many seasons it publishes. MERGE THE ARRAYS across its round-ups into ONE record.
3. CONFLICT OF INTEREST ON THE AWARD. Jewish News CREATED the British Kebab Awards' kosher category in 2022 and co-runs it. Its coverage of that award is not an independent opinion about the winner - see awardBodiesChecked, trap 2.

AND ONE PATH TO AVOID: /spotlight/ IS SPONSORED CONTENT. 'A Taste of Excellence: Inside One Ashbourne' sits at /spotlight/a-taste-of-excellence-inside-one-ashbourne/. Advertorial on a real masthead is still advertorial - it is tier F wearing a newspaper's masthead, the same call caribbean.json made on The Voice's /sponsored-2/ path. NEVER COUNT A /spotlight/ URL. Its ordinary reviews and round-ups are a different matter.

Per trap 5, DO NOT reconstruct an @handle from any of them - a display name is not a handle, and three TikTok sources on pizza were dropped for exactly this. Read the real handle off the channel page at collection, and match the casing already in data/sources.json (trap 3).

  STRONGEST CANDIDATES - London-specific, food-first:
    'Food Review Club'      2026, 24,637 views - 'We Found GOLDERS GREEN's VIRAL Kosher Street Food Spot'
    'The Hungry Brown Boy'  2026, 34,961 views - 'I Survived 24 Hours Eating Only Jewish & Kosher Food in London'
    'EATOUTGUIDELONDON'     2025, 114 views    - 'Fresh, Kosher & Full of Surprises - Soyo Golders Green Review'. Tiny audience; per trap 1 that is irrelevant to tiering.
    'The Sacred Jungle'     2022, 770 views    - 'Carmelli Kosher bakery in the North London'

  ASSESS BEFORE COUNTING - London, but community tourism rather than restaurant criticism:
    'Big Japa'  2025, 11,356 views - 'Exploring London's most strict JEWISH community!'
    'YESMAN'    2025, 46,935 views - 'Exploring London's Most JEWISH Borough!'
  THESE ARE NOT RESTAURANT REVIEWS AND THEY SHOULD PROBABLY NOT BE COUNTED AS ONE. A video touring a religious neighbourhood is a different thing from a video about where to eat, it will name few venues if any, and treating a Charedi community as sightseeing is not a voice this guide wants to borrow authority from. Watch them before deciding; the presumption is out.

  OUT ON SCOPE: 'Living Lchaim' and 'DansDeals' (US/worldwide, not London), 'Best Ever Food Review Show' (1.76M views but establish the city before counting - trap 12 at 1.7 million views is still trap 12), 'i24NEWS English' (news), 'shiezoli' (news report about a restaurant being vandalised - not an opinion about the food, and it would be grotesque to count it as one), 'Barnet Council' (a local authority's community film, not a food creator), 'mazaltovvideo.com' (a 2014 trade expo).

EXTRACTION WARNING FROM THE ACTUAL RUN: chapter markers on the one video that had them were emoji-prefixed and came back as replacement characters, and the script's 'venues' were chapter titles like 'Intro', 'Jewish Bagels' and 'Thanks & Peace!!' - trap 8 with a venue-shaped surface. Decode entities and emoji before anything looks at a name (trap 9), and print the name list per source before printing a source count.
theSourceMixVerdict:
THE FLOOR IS TECHNICALLY REACHABLE AND REACHING IT WOULD NOT MAKE THIS A CONSENSUS GUIDE. Read theViabilityVerdict first; this section only answers the narrower audit question.

THE FLOOR: no judged award exists (the British Kebab Awards' kosher category is not one - see awardBodiesChecked), so scripts/audit-source-mix.mjs requires THREE independent social voices rather than two.

  TIER A  0 and unfillable.
  TIER B  3  The Jewish Chronicle, Jewish News, DesignMyNight. TWO ARE UNREGISTERED and need adding to data/sources.json.
  TIER C  3  London x London (3.5 years old), UK Jewish Life (borderline, unregistered), Walk Eat London (no byline, no date, 40% non-kosher).
  TIER D  AVAILABLE at no cost. Four defensible London candidates found - see theVideoFinding. 3 of 3 is achievable but only just, and two of the four have tiny audiences.
  TIER E  BLOCKED. Reddit refuses curl and the browser pane alike. Only Rob pasting thread URLs fixes it.

SO THE AUDIT WOULD PASS AND THE GUIDE WOULD STILL BE WRONG-SHAPED. That is the thing worth recording, because a green audit is exactly what would persuade someone to ship this as a ranked guide. Six editorial domains over a field of roughly forty restaurants is not a consensus; it is four listicles and two community papers, and the four listicles name the same ten venues because those are the ten with a website.

THE CONVERGENCE IS MEASURABLE AND IT IS THE PROOF. Across DesignMyNight (10), London x London (11) and UK Jewish Life (17), the SAME names recur: Reubens, Novellino, Tish, Hummus Bar, Pita, Met Su Yan, Delicatessen, Slice. Roughly eight venues carry most of the citations in the topic while the KLBD register alone lists 39. A citation-ranked guide would print those eight and bury thirty-one certified restaurants that no listicle happened to mention - including every Stamford Hill venue, which is the part of the scene that is least written about and most in need of a guide.

AND THE ONE-SHAPED-CORPUS PROBLEM NO SCRIPT CATCHES. audit-source-mix flags a corpus over 70% SOCIAL. It does not flag one where three of six published sources carry no certification information at all, one has no byline or date, and the two best are community papers that do not rank. That is this corpus, and this file is the only place that says so.
theRankingProblem:
NOT ONE SOURCE IN THIS TOPIC PUBLISHES A QUALITY RANKING. Section 1 of the standard article shape - 'The winners: the venues that actually top a ranking' - has nothing to lead with, and SKILL.md forbids substituting citation count for it.

  The Jewish Chronicle   reviews and seasonal round-ups. No ranks.
  Jewish News            seasonal round-ups. No ranks.
  DesignMyNight          thematic selection of 10. No ranks.
  London x London        11, unordered. No ranks.
  UK Jewish Life         numbered 1-17, but nothing in the text defines an order. Probably unordered - re-read the caption before recording a single rank (trap 11).
  Walk Eat London        'Top 10', unordered, and four of the ten are not kosher.
  British Kebab Awards   ORDERED in the sense that it has a winner - but part public vote, one dish, UK-wide. Not a ranking of restaurants.

THE ONLY ORDERED FACT AVAILABLE IS THE KEBAB AWARD, and it covers one dish. RECOMMEND: drop section 1 entirely and open on the structure the reader actually needs - meat or dairy, which area, open when - with the award mentioned as a dated fact inside Mazal's and Reubens' entries. Do not invent an order, and do not let 'cited by 3 sources' stand in for one.

facetAxis.note:
THE AXIS IS MEAT / DAIRY / PARVE, AND IT IS THE CERTIFIER'S OWN FIELD RATHER THAN ONE THIS PROJECT CHOSE. KLBD labels all 39 of its restaurant entries this way and no other axis in the topic is published by anybody.

IT IS ALSO THE ONLY AXIS THAT ANSWERS A QUESTION THE READER CANNOT ANSWER FOR THEMSELVES. A kosher kitchen is meat or dairy, never both, so the label determines the entire menu: no cheese in a meat restaurant, no meat in a dairy one, and no cream, butter or milky coffee after a meat meal. A reader who wants a burger and a reader who wants a pizza are choosing between different buildings. Nothing on the frontage says which, and the two Novellinos sit 100 metres apart on the same road with different answers.

WHY NOT THE ALTERNATIVES, each rejected on evidence:
  CUISINE - considered, and it is a genuine second axis rather than the primary one. The register spans Israeli grills, sushi, Chinese (Kaifeng), Italian, burgers, poke, smokehouse and pizza, which is real variety. But with roughly 40 venues across 8 cuisines, most values would hold two or three venues, and a reader still cannot tell whether the sushi place serves meat. Carry cuisine as a SECONDARY tag, not the axis.
  AREA - rejected because there is barely an axis to build. Golders Green, Hendon, Temple Fortune and Edgware are one contiguous corridor in Barnet and hold the large majority of the field. An area split would be one enormous bucket and five singletons. It belongs as a short cross-reference section, and the honest line in it is that a reader in south or east London has almost nothing.
  CERTIFYING AUTHORITY - rejected AS AN AXIS on principle, not on data. Structuring the guide by hechsher would organise the page around a communal disagreement this site has no standing in, and would read as ranking the authorities. Carry it as a per-venue FIELD - see theDistinctions axis 4.
  PRICE - the field is narrow and mostly mid-range. The standard Cheapest section covers it.

values.label: Meat (fleishig)
values.describeAs: grills, schnitzel, shawarma and salt beef, cooked with no dairy anywhere in the building - so no cheese, no butter and no milk in the coffee afterwards

values.label: Dairy (milchig)
values.describeAs: pizza, pasta, bagels, fish and cheesecake, in a kitchen that serves no meat at all

values.label: Parve and fish
values.describeAs: neither meat nor dairy - the sushi counters and poke bars, which is what makes them the one place a mixed group can all eat

facetAxis.checkBeforePrinting: PARVE IS THE THIN ONE AND IT IS ALSO SLIPPERY. Only four KLBD entries carry a parve label and every one of them is written 'Meat/Parev' rather than parve alone - SurFin Poke, Sushi Haven x2, Sushi Hinoki. So these are MEAT establishments serving parve food, not parve establishments, and describing them as parve would be wrong. VERIFY WHAT 'Meat/Parev' MEANS AT THE VENUE before writing the section, and if it collapses, fold these into the meat value and drop parve to a sentence. Do not print a three-venue section built on a label nobody checked.
facetAxis.considerAdding: THE BAKERIES, DELIS AND TAKEAWAY COUNTERS ARE A LARGE PART OF THIS SCENE AND THEY ARE ON DIFFERENT REGISTERS. KLBD publishes /kosher-places/bakeries/ and /kosher-places/delis-shops-pop-ups/ separately from restaurants, and SKA's licensees are mostly delis and cafés. Carmelli in Golders Green is one of the best-known kosher food businesses in London and is a BAKERY, so it appears on no restaurant list in this pass and on one video. DECIDE THE SCOPE BEFORE COLLECTING - a restaurants-only guide is defensible and would be smaller and cleaner; a guide covering the bakeries and delis is closer to how people actually eat in these neighbourhoods. Whichever is chosen, say so on the page.

formatSection.title: Closed for Shabbat: when you can actually eat
formatSection.note:
THE SECTION NO COMPETITOR PRINTS AND THE ONE THAT DECIDES WHETHER THE TRIP HAPPENS. A supervised kosher restaurant shuts for Shabbat - from Friday afternoon until after nightfall on Saturday - and that removes Friday dinner and Saturday lunch, the two busiest restaurant sessions of the week in London. It also closes for Jewish festivals, whose dates move every year because the calendar is lunar. A reader planning a Saturday night dinner in Golders Green needs this before they need to know what is good.

THE ABSENCE IS VERIFIED, NOT ASSUMED. Of the six editorial sources in this topic, exactly ONE mentions Shabbat closing at all, and only for a single venue: DesignMyNight notes Novellino closes 'with the exception of the Sabbath and Jewish festivals'. London x London mentions Shabbat only as a meal Tish serves. UK Jewish Life mentions it once, as 'Shabbat ordering' at Deli 98. The JC, Jewish News and Walk Eat London print nothing usable. So five of six sources write about kosher restaurants without telling a reader the days they are shut.

THE DATA EXISTS AND IT IS NOT IN ANY LISTICLE. It is on the venues' own sites - Novellino's says 'Apart from the Jewish Sabbath and festivals, Novellino is open everyday for breakfast, lunch and dinner' - and occasionally in the register itself, where KLBD's White Fish entry reads 'Eat in and take away Sun-Thurs 12-10pm. Fri take away only.' That is a per-venue browser pass, and it is the single highest-value piece of legwork in the topic.

SATURDAY NIGHT IS THE INTERESTING HALF AND THE HARD HALF. Shabbat ends at nightfall, which is around 5pm in December and after 10pm in June, so a venue's Saturday opening MOVES BY FIVE HOURS ACROSS THE YEAR. A fixed time would be wrong for most of the year. Say that it opens after nightfall and that the time moves with the season; point the reader at their own check rather than printing an hour.

NEVER ESTIMATE, INFER OR CALCULATE ONE OF THESE TIMES. Do not compute sunset. Do not assume every certified venue closes - a takeaway counter under some supervisions may operate differently, and 'they're all shut on Saturday' is exactly the kind of thing that feels safe to assume and is wrong per venue. Where it cannot be confirmed from the venue or the register, print that the venue closes for Shabbat WITHOUT a time. And do NOT print festival dates without checking them for the year of publication - a wrong festival date is a wasted journey and it is also the kind of error that tells a Jewish reader the writer does not know the subject.

WHY NOT THE OTHER CANDIDATES. CERTIFIED VERSUS KOSHER-STYLE was the obvious one and it is rejected as a SECTION for a good reason: it is not a section, it is a per-venue field that must appear on EVERY entry, and demoting it to one part of the page would imply the rest of the guide had not applied it. See theDistinctions axis 1. MEAT VERSUS DAIRY is the facet axis and already structures the guide. WHICH AUTHORITY CERTIFIES IT is a field, and making it a section would read as ranking the authorities.

sectionPlan:
THE STANDARD ORDER IN SKILL.md DOES NOT FIT THIS TOPIC AND SHOULD NOT BE FORCED ONTO IT. Recommended shape, for a human to approve before drafting:

  DROP SECTION 1 ('The winners'). Nothing ranks. See theRankingProblem.
  OPEN INSTEAD ON THE THREE FACTS A READER CANNOT GET ELSEWHERE: how small and how concentrated the scene is, that meat and dairy are separate buildings, and that everything shuts for Shabbat.
  THEN THE FACET AXIS - meat, dairy, parve - as the main body, with the certifying authority and the Shabbat fact on every entry.
  THEN AREA, as a short cross-reference, saying honestly that this is a Barnet scene with six or seven outliers.
  THEN the format section - Closed for Shabbat.
  THEN bakeries, delis and takeaway counters IF the scope decision in facetAxis.considerAdding includes them.
  THEN new openings - KLBD's dated monthly update PDFs are the best source on this site for any topic's new openings, because they are dated, primary and complete.
  THEN booking and FAQs, which on this topic should carry the festival warning.

AND CARRY A VISIBLE 'CERTIFICATION CHECKED ON <date>' LINE. Not a weakness line - a currency line, the same way an award carries a year. A licence is perishable and the reader is entitled to know how fresh the check is. Confirm the wording with Rob, since it is close to the forbidden shape and must not read as hedging.
knownGaps: NO JUDGED KOSHER RESTAURANT AWARD EXISTS. Tier A is empty and cannot be filled. The British Kebab Awards' kosher category is part public vote, judges one dish, and is UK-wide - real and dated, but not a restaurant ranking. See awardBodiesChecked.

KEDASSIA PUBLISHES NO REACHABLE REGISTER AND THIS IS THE BIGGEST HOLE IN THE TOPIC. kedassia.org.uk does not resolve at all (DNS failure, 2026-09-07). Kedassia is the strictly-Orthodox authority most associated with STAMFORD HILL, so the least-documented certifier governs the least-written-about part of the scene. Its licensees are visible only through third-party directories, which are not the authority. ASK, or find the register by phone - do not infer a Kedassia hechsher from a directory.

TIME OUT AND THE INFATUATION PUBLISH NO LONDON KOSHER GUIDE AT ALL. Verified by direct search 2026-09-07. Time Out carries 46 source records across this site, more than any other domain, and none here. This is the sourcing problem in one line and it is why the SERP fills with directories.
